Developed by: BLACK HOLE STUDIO GOA Who is Prince Yadav? How Delhi pacer became India’s trusted death-overs specialist
 By Team Herald Published: 1 November 2026 Share SHARE Prince Yadav’s journey from playing tennis-ball cricket on dusty grounds in Delhi’s outskirts to becoming one of India’s trusted death-over bowlers is a story of pace, persistence and precision. The 24-year-old fast bowler from Najafgarh has carried the lessons of his early cricketing days into international cricket, making his yorkers a formidable weapon in the shortest format.
 Yadav credits tennis-ball cricket for developing the arm speed that has become central to his bowling. Unlike conventional cricket balls, tennis and tape balls offer little movement in the air or off the surface, forcing bowlers to depend on pace and accurate yorkers to trouble batters.

 He also trained with wet tennis balls, which became heavier during Delhi’s dew-covered evenings. The additional weight helped him prepare for match conditions and develop the strength needed to bowl fast yorkers consistently.
 That early experience has shaped his approach in T20 cricket. Yadav has emerged as a specialist at the death, delivering yorkers at speeds frequently exceeding 140 kmph and using low full tosses as an alternative when he misses his intended length.
 His numbers underline his effectiveness. Across 10 overs bowled between the 16th and 20th overs in the format, he has conceded just under 10 runs per over while picking up five wickets. Remarkably, batters have managed only one six against him during those overs.
 Yadav’s yorkers are effective because of his ability to vary their line without compromising pace. He frequently targets the base of the off-stump or just outside it, while also possessing the ability to bowl wide yorkers and deliveries aimed at middle and off.
 - Advertisement - Unlike many fast bowlers, he rarely relies on slower yorkers, which carry a greater margin for error. Instead, he trusts his pace to prevent batters from anticipating his deliveries and attempting unconventional shots.
 Even when he misses the perfect yorker length, Yadav generally produces a low full toss rather than a hittable good-length delivery. This makes it difficult for batters to capitalise on his occasional errors.
 His tactical understanding is equally important. Yadav often has a say in setting his own field, placing third man and fine leg deep to account for edges while leaving the mid-wicket region relatively open. His confidence in executing yorkers allows him to dictate where batters can score.
 During India’s recent T20 matches against New Zealand, Yadav was entrusted with bowling the final over by captain Shreyas Iyer. Across the two matches, he conceded very little, with Michael Bracewell managing a boundary through an attempted scoop over the wicketkeeper.
 - Advertisement - His ability to remain composed under pressure has impressed India’s bowling coach Morne Morkel. The former South African fast bowler praised Yadav’s mindset, highlighting his calmness in difficult situations and his ability to deliver when the team needs him.
 Yadav’s attacking philosophy is another defining feature. Rather than focusing solely on restricting runs, he looks to take wickets even during the final overs. He has previously expressed confidence in his ability to bowl six yorkers in an over without being discouraged if one turns into a full toss.
 The 24-year-old has also expanded his bowling repertoire since moving from tennis-ball cricket to the conventional leather ball. He has developed an effective outswinger and demonstrated his ability to produce decisive deliveries against established batters.
 One of his memorable breakthroughs came in the Indian Premier League, when he bowled Virat Kohli with a delivery that initially appeared to be an outswinger before moving back towards the stumps.
 However, it is the yorker that remains the foundation of Yadav’s success. From the dusty grounds of Najafgarh to India’s international dressing room, the lessons of tennis-ball cricket continue to define the fast bowler’s rise as a specialist in the death overs.
